Lesson overview:
- Level: A1 General English
- Unit: MODULE 3. OBJECTS & PERSONAL SPACE
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: 3.2 Possessions
- Materials: vocabulary cards, audio, reading handout
Warm-up: say one word you already know for this topic.
Recycles everyday objects from Lesson 3.1.
Recycled language: clothes, devices, furniture.
Answer from memory: which word belongs to this topic?
Which word belongs to this topic?
Core Active Vocabulary (4 items):

clothes — the things you wear. Example: My clothes are in the wardrobe.
devices — machines such as phones and laptops. Example: I have got three devices.
furniture — tables, chairs, beds and similar things. Example: The furniture is in my flat.
personal belongings — the things that belong to you. Example: My personal belongings are in this bag.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• Have you got a ...?
• I have got a ...
• I haven't got a ...
• These are my belongings.
• It is mine.

Grammar focus: Have / have got.
Use have got for possession: I have got a laptop. Question: Have you got a charger? Negative: I haven't got a car.
Controlled practice: choose the correct option.
Choose the correct sentence.
Choose the correct negative.
options: I not have got a car.

Reading: read the text and answer the questions.
My personal belongings are in two bags. I have got a laptop, a phone and a camera. My clothes are in the wardrobe and the furniture is in my flat.
